result.title: AURA 2.0: From User-Driven Responses to Model-Initiated Conversations in Streaming Video
result.summary: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) enables the model to invoke external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporate returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities. We open-source the model weights and inference code.

AI.brief_summary: AURA 2.0 构建了一个流式视频大模型系统，在原有 AURA 基础上加入「模型主动发起对话」、基于当前视觉与对话上下文的流式工具调用、双向交互式视觉定位，并用长时程交互记忆维持跨长视频的上下文连续性，配套自建流式交互数据集与三阶段训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及 latent 推理状态，但其「何时主动开口」的触发策略、按需调用外部工具补充证据、以及长时程记忆维持状态，可为 LVR 中 STOP 时机的判定、LOOK 式证据获取与跨步状态携带提供可核查的工程线索。
